text:
UTA arrives as the team creating the better chances. It generates 3.68 expected goals per 60 and allows 2.83, and it has taken 58% of the expected goals at five on five, against 53% for EDM. EDM's numbers are quieter at both ends (3.15 for, 2.33 against), yet it scores 4.83 goals a game to UTA's 3.86. The model sees a close game, projecting 3.11 expected goals for UTA and 2.93 for EDM. Special teams lean EDM: its power play produces 0.98 expected goals a game and its penalty kill allows 0.48, while UTA sits at 0.91 and 0.58. UTA also takes 5.0 penalties a game, which keeps handing the other side power plays.

In net, projected starters Karel Vejmelka (UTA) and Devon Levi (EDM) both have thin samples. Vejmelka is at +1.71 goals saved above expected over six games this season and +5.39 across 64 games last year. Levi is at -0.24 over four games, with no last-season figure to lean on.

EDM is 5-0-0 in its last five with 57% of the expected goals, though it lost the chance battle in two of the wins, including 43% in its most recent game at LAK. UTA is 3-2-0 with 56%, and its 1-6 loss at BOS came with 66% of the expected goals. The model likes Connor McDavid (40% to score, 42% for two or more points) and Leon Draisaitl (39% to score) for EDM, and Dylan Guenther (34%) and Nick Schmaltz (33%) for UTA.
